- When sentiment turns bullish (↑) after a downtrend, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- After strong sentiment spikes (≥0.67), model often overestimates continuation — apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment volatility is high (frequent ±0.5+ swings), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecasts with 3-day moving average.
- When news volume spikes (≥2.0) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underreacts — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast.
- Model consistently underestimates true price during mean-reversion phases — if 3-day MA of history is > forecast, adjust forecast upward by 1–2%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 1–3 days — if true outcome is rising, forecast should be 1–2% higher than 1-day prior.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is low, model underestimates downside risk — add 0.5–1.5% downward bias.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common — if forecast > true outcome by >2%, reduce by 1–3% for next 5 days.
